chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"Rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose are among what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله established as sunnah (prophetic tradition)."

The Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—said: Whoever washes his face and his forearms once each has fulfilled the obligation; and if he washes these limbs twice, he thereby attains reward, gains additional merit, and completes his wudu (ablution) thoroughly.
And what indicates that is His, Exalted is He, saying:
"When you rise for salat (prayer), wash your faces and your hands."

And whoever washes his face and his forearms once has entered into compliance with what the apparent wording requires. Whatever exceeds that needs a shar'i proof, and there is no proof here that what exceeds that is obligatory; and that too is indicated by this.

key_terms.أَجْرًا: Reward granted for performing an additional meritorious act.
key_terms.الِاسْتِنْشَاقُ: Drawing water into the nose as part of the sunnah (prophetic tradition) acts of purification.
key_terms.الْوَاجِبَ: The obligatory requirement that must be fulfilled.
key_terms.فَضْلًا: Extra merit or virtue beyond the minimum obligation.
key_terms.وُضُوءَهُ: His wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer).

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, is washing the limbs once in wudu (ablution) sufficient, and what is the ruling on rinsing the mouth and nose?
ai.summary: This passage explains that rinsing the mouth and sniffing water into the nose are from the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, while washing the face and forearms once in wudu (ablution) fulfills the obligatory requirement. Washing these limbs twice brings reward and added merit, but the text argues from the Quran that any washing beyond once is not established here as obligatory.
